extracted.intended_audience: administrative law practitioners, UIC staff, claimants and their representatives (appeals participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria governing appeals to the Umpire under the Unemployment Insurance Act, including filing, file composition, hearings, evidence, representation, timelines and the Umpire's decision-making powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to obtain leave to appeal (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain appellants must obtain leave to appeal from the chairman of the Board of referees before bringing the appeal to the Umpire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave must be requested within 30 days (sec. 96(1) and reg.183(1)); chairman must notify the UIC of his decision within 15 days; even if chairman grants leave at the end of that period (45 days after Board decision) the right of appeal does not lapse because an application for leave is regarded as the equivalent of filing an appeal. The chairman's authority is conferred ex officio and cannot be delegated to a member or another chairman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for ordinary appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal time for appeal is within sixty days of the day the claimant is notified of the decision (sec. 98).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there's dispute over the mailing/receipt date, UIC certification that the Board decision was sent by mail is evidence that it was received in the ordinary course (sec.120(2)). Only the Umpire may extend the sixty-day deadline for special reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of UIC-filed appeal on benefit payments
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal filed by the UIC can result in withholding of benefits in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withholding applies where the UIC's appeal is based on sec.44 (labour dispute) or that the Board failed to take into account an applicable provision of the Act or Regulations, but only if the appeal is filed within 21 days of the Board's decision. If the Umpire rejects the UIC's appeal, withheld benefits are paid retroactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the claimant's appeal file
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant's file forwarded to the Regional Office and Umpire must contain the application for benefit and all supporting documentation and records of prior proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File should include: application for benefit, supporting documentation, additional information gathered by Agents II or Benefit Control Officers, the appeal to the Board of referees, the Board's decision, and, for labour disputes, documentation compiled by Agent II and transcripts of statements before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment of leave and grounds to notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where leave to appeal was required and granted, the leave and the statement of grounds must be attached to the notice of appeal and placed on the claimant's file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents become part of the file forwarded to Regional Office and eventually to the Umpire; they start procedural consequences such as the docketing and triggering other time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: UIC regional office responsibilities (observations and docketing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Offices prepare the UIC's written observations and assemble the Umpire dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg.184(4) recognizes the UIC's right to file written observations. Regional Offices must attach the complete text of Umpire caselaw cited, may apply to the Umpire for a hearing (reg.185(1) and (4)), and can request the Umpire to summon the appellant (sec.100 and reg.185(5)). Since April 1976, reg.184(3) sets a 60-day limit for the UIC to make up and forward the appeal docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and timing for filing observations and requesting hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of the UIC docket triggers the fifteen-day period for parties and interested third parties to file observations and apply for a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg.184(5) and reg.185(3) — the Umpire must grant a hearing whenever applied for (reg.185(1)); if no hearing is applied for, reg.184(7) empowers the Umpire to decide on the basis of documents filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar's pre-hearing summary and scheduling duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar prepares a factual and legal summary for the Umpire and organizes practical arrangements for hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary length varies between two and fifteen pages and may indicate a recommended solution without prejudice. The registrar waits to collect appeals from a region to concentrate hearings in major cities, plans itineraries, respects claimant's official language choice, and gives 14 days' notice of hearing to appellant, the Commission and third parties (reg.185(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's procedural discretion and residual jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire determines the procedure at the hearing and is not bound by legal or technical rules of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec.93(1) directs informality and expedition 'as the circumstances and consideration of fairness will permit.' Reg.185(7) grants residual jurisdiction: 'The procedure at the hearing... shall be determined by the umpire.' The Umpire may shorten and simplify procedure as he thinks fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public nature and court-like setting of hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings before the Umpire are public and often have a court-like staffing and setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearings attended by registrar/deputy registrar/assistants (clerk functions) and usher; Umpires prefer Federal Court premises or other courtrooms, but do not sit in UIC offices to avoid compromising impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation in degree of formality among Umpires
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual Umpires set their own tone for hearings, ranging from highly formal to open discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three schools: (1) solemn/trial-like with strict procedural technicalities; (2) direct pragmatic approach — open structured discussion; (3) compromise — maintain formality but simplify using sec.93(1) to reduce adversarial aspects. Degree of formality may be adjusted for self-represented claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for self-represented claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: When claimants appear without counsel, the Umpire should explain rules or tolerate deviations so long as the logic of debate is preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Umpire may simplify or relax cross-examination requirements and other technicalities to avoid confusing the claimant; fairness and preservation of debate logic are guiding concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative merits of types of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Different types of claimant representation have differing procedural and substantive advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union representatives and lay advocates often have an advantage over (non-specialist) lawyers in substantive knowledge of unemployment insurance; legal aid lawyers who specialize may match lawyers' procedural skills. The UIC is always represented by lawyers from its Legal Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's focus in review (legal reasoning vs factual findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire's review is directed primarily at the legal reasoning of the Board of referees rather than its factual findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, because transcripts or reports of Board hearings are generally unavailable (except labour disputes), Umpires often re-examine cases based on items in the file and party statements; Board decisions are often insufficiently justified, making this difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's power to rule on procedural incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire rules on issues like party interest, third-party standing, late appeals, and extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He decides whether associations meet sec.97 conditions to file appeals, rules on direct interest of third parties (reg.184(6)), accepts or refuses late appeals and may grant extensions; he must stay proceedings if issues fall under the Minister of National Revenue (sec.105) until Minister decides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing typically follows a court-like sequence: statements, cross-examination, witness examination, summing-up, pleadings and answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory rules exist only for limited aspects: reimbursement of persons requested to appear (sec.101 and reg.185(5)), privilege for evidence providers (sec.115). Sec.114's effect on UIC disclosure before the Umpire is unclear. The Umpire may shorten/simplify the procedure under sec.93(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's decision form and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire must render a written decision and typically takes some weeks to prepare it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg.186(1) requires written decisions. In the sample period the average time to write and forward the decision was five weeks and two days. Decisions may uphold, rescind, amend, or remit (send back) the Board's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Umpire's remedial powers (overpayments/write-offs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire cannot order write-offs under reg.175 but may recommend or urge the UIC to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing-off recoverable overpayments is a UIC prerogative; Umpires often urge write-offs based on claimant means, technical errors by UIC, delay in detection, or absence of fraudulent intent — instances recorded in sample decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of decision outcomes and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision outcomes are recorded as upheld, rescinded, amended, or sent back; UIC statistics may only reflect upheld/rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample statistics showed proportions for each outcome; authors note some discrepancy (e.g., remitted cases may be undercounted in UIC stats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's authority to decide on documents-only cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no hearing is applied for, the Umpire may render decision based on the documents filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg.184(7) empowers the Umpire to decide on the basis of documents if there is no hearing; practice shows a substantial proportion of appeals are decided strictly on the file (about one-third in the sample).
